questions.question: You are writing a Python client application for an agent in a Microsoft Foundry project. Which class should you use to connect to the project?

options.text: AIProjectClient
options.why: Correct. AIProjectClient from azure-ai-projects connects to a Foundry project endpoint.

options.text: TextAnalyticsClient
options.why: TextAnalyticsClient calls Azure Language text analysis features, not agents.

options.text: SpeechRecognizer
options.why: SpeechRecognizer converts speech to text in the Speech SDK.

options.text: BlobServiceClient
options.why: BlobServiceClient works with Azure Blob Storage.

questions.explanation: The Foundry SDK's AIProjectClient connects to the project and provides access to agents and an OpenAI client.

questions.scenario: A client application sends a user's first question to an agent. The user then asks a follow-up question that refers to the first answer, but the agent responds as if it has no context.
questions.question: What should you change in the application?

options.text: Increase the temperature of the model deployment.
options.why: Temperature affects randomness, not conversation memory.

options.text: Create one conversation and pass the same conversation ID with each request.
options.why: Correct. The conversation stores the history, so later turns have the earlier context.

options.text: Create a new agent version before each request.
options.why: New versions do not carry conversation history and would clutter the version list.

options.text: Switch the deployment type to Global Batch.
options.why: Batch deployments process requests asynchronously and do not provide chat context.

questions.explanation: Reusing the same conversation ID across responses.create calls keeps multi-turn context.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about authenticating AIProjectClient are true?

options.text: It supports Microsoft Entra ID authentication, such as DefaultAzureCredential.
options.why: Correct. Entra ID is the supported authentication method.

options.text: On a developer workstation, DefaultAzureCredential can use the identity from az login.
options.why: Correct. DefaultAzureCredential tries several sources, including the Azure CLI sign-in.

options.text: It requires the resource API key to be embedded in the code.
options.why: AIProjectClient does not use API keys, and keys should never be embedded in code.

options.text: It requires a shared access signature (SAS) token.
options.why: SAS tokens are used with Azure Storage, not with Foundry projects.

questions.explanation: AIProjectClient authenticates with Microsoft Entra ID. DefaultAzureCredential uses az login locally or a managed identity in Azure.

questions.question: Which method creates an agent, or a new version of an existing agent, from Python code by using the Foundry SDK?

options.text: project.agents.create_version
options.why: Correct. create_version with a PromptAgentDefinition creates an agent version.

options.text: project.deployments.create
options.why: Deployments relate to models, not to agent definitions.

options.text: openai.images.generate
options.why: This method generates images.

options.text: client.analyze_sentiment
options.why: This method belongs to the Azure Language text analytics client.

questions.explanation: project.agents.create_version takes an agent name and a PromptAgentDefinition and returns a new immutable version.

questions.question: In a PromptAgentDefinition, what value should you provide for the model parameter?

options.text: The name of the model deployment in the Foundry project
options.why: Correct. The model parameter refers to your deployment name.

options.text: The name of the Azure subscription
options.why: The subscription is not referenced in the agent definition.

options.text: The resource group that contains the Foundry resource
options.why: The resource group is not part of the agent definition.

options.text: The URL of the model card
options.why: Model cards are documentation and are not used to call a model.

questions.explanation: Foundry SDK calls refer to models by the deployment name that you chose when you deployed the model.
